name: Motorized Bicycle
description: Iowa's moped: a motor vehicle with a seat and no more than three wheels that can't go faster than 39 mph on level ground without pedaling. The definition names no engine type and sets no power limit, so an electric two- or three-wheeler that exceeds the low-speed electric bicycle limits but tops out at 39 mph is one. Defined by Iowa Code §321.1(40)(b).
restrictions: A saddle or seat, and no more than three wheels on the ground; pedals are optional
Can't go faster than 39 mph on level ground without pedaling; there is no limit on motor power
A low-speed electric bicycle is excluded; an electric bike over 750 watts, or one assisting past its class speed, is a motorized bicycle when it can't exceed 39 mph
Its manufacturer's certificate of origin must state its top speed, and the DOT may test a model it suspects can exceed 39 mph and refuse to register it as a motorized bicycle
Riders need a driver's license: any class works, or a motorized-bicycle-only license from age 14 after a vision test and written rules-of-the-road test
An applicant under 16 for a motorized-bicycle-only license must first complete an approved motorized bicycle education course, and that license is canceled on any moving-violation conviction
Titled and registered with the county treasurer for $7 a year, and carries a motorcycle-size plate
Must carry financial liability coverage, with proof on board, to be driven on a highway
Can't carry a passenger on a highway, and the rider must sit astride the seat facing forward
Must keep a headlamp lit and fly a triangular Day-Glo bicycle safety flag at least 5 feet off the ground on any highway
No more than two abreast in a lane, and no riding between lanes or rows of traffic
